Identify nontrivial constraints

Source: R/screening-nontrivial.R
nontrivial_screen.Rd

Exact screen of the constraints of each district (Proposition 4 of the paper). An equality constraint is trivial if it holds for every strictly positive distribution that satisfies the conditional independencies implied by the graph. These are the linear combinations of the normalization constraints and of the constraints saying that, for every set S of members that contains all members that are ancestors of its members, the margin of S under the intervention does not depend on the external parents of the other members. An inequality constraint is trivial if it is implied by the probability simplex together with the equality constraints of its district. This is the case if and only if some probability is zero at every vertex of the district polytope on its facet, and then the constraint is a nonnegativity constraint written in a different form. A nontrivial inequality constraint is violated by some strictly positive distribution that satisfies the conditional independencies and every other constraint.

Usage

nontrivial_screen(dhvm, drels, dpoly, tol = 1e-09)

Arguments

dhvm

An object of class `dhvm`, see [dhvm()], with c-degree at most 1

drels

A list of relations as returned by [dhvm_linear_relations()] applied to `dhvm`

dpoly

The polytopes as returned by [dhvm_relations_to_polytope()] applied to `drels`. Which vertices lie on which facet is computed in exact rational arithmetic from its `HrepQ` element, or, if that is missing, from `Hrep` converted with [rcdd::d2q()].

tol

Numeric tolerance for the ranks in the screen of the equality constraints

Value

A named list of logical vectors, one for each district, with one element per row of the H-representation. For an inequality constraint it is `TRUE` if the constraint is nontrivial. For the equality constraints, the rows marked `TRUE` form a basis of the nontrivial ones: together with the conditional independencies they imply all equality constraints of the district.

Details

Unlike [prob_simplex_screen()], the result does not depend on how the rows of the H-representation are written, and it flags no trivial constraints.

Examples

xab <- dhvm(caugi(X %-->% A, Y %-->% B, U %-->% A + B))
rels <- dhvm_linear_relations(xab)
poly <- dhvm_relations_to_polytope(rels)
nt <- nontrivial_screen(xab, rels, poly)
## the 8 CHSH inequalities
hrep_to_text(poly$Hrep[[1]], rels$probstarform[[1]])[nt[[1]]]
#> [1] "P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 0) + P*(A = 0,B = 1|X = 1,Y = 0) + P*(A = 1,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 1) - P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 1) <= 1"                                                             
#> [2] "P*(A = 0,B = 1|X = 0,Y = 0) + P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 0) + P*(A = 1,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 1) - P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 1) <= 1"                                                             
#> [3] "P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 0) + P*(A = 1,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 0) + P*(A = 0,B = 1|X = 0,Y = 0) - P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 0) - P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 1) + P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 1) <= 1" 
#> [4] "P*(A = 1,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 0) + P*(A = 0,B = 1|X = 1,Y = 0) + P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 1) - P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 1) <= 1"                                                             
#> [5] "-P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 0) - P*(A = 0,B = 1|X = 1,Y = 0) - P*(A = 1,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 1) + P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 1) <= 0"                                                            
#> [6] "-P*(A = 0,B = 1|X = 0,Y = 0) - P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 0) - P*(A = 1,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 1) + P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 1) <= 0"                                                            
#> [7] "-P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 0) - P*(A = 1,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 0) - P*(A = 0,B = 1|X = 0,Y = 0) + P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 0) + P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 1) - P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 1) <= 0"
#> [8] "-P*(A = 1,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 0) - P*(A = 0,B = 1|X = 1,Y = 0) - P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 0,Y = 1) + P*(A = 0,B = 0|X = 1,Y = 1) <= 0"
